tools.name: account_plan_builder
tools.description: Helps you decide how to grow an account in the next 90 days. You give the account name, plus contacts, products, threats and notes if you have them. You get a strategic account plan: a power map with one row per contact you name, whitespace analysis, competitive questions, an answer for each objection and a 90 day plan. It does not look the account up.

current_arr.description: Current ARR with this account (0 for prospects)

known_contacts.description: Known contacts and their roles, one per line or separated by semicolons, for example: Head of RevOps (champion); CFO. Each entry becomes one row, so put other notes in account notes

current_products.description: Products/services they currently use from you

account_notes.description: Any additional context about the account

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Account Plan Builder

tools.name: deal_strategy_coach
tools.description: Helps you decide what to do next to move a deal. You give the deal name and stage, plus competitors, stakeholder positions and blockers. You get a deal health score, a strategy for the stage, next steps and risks to handle. Ask the user to confirm blocker status, economic buyer engagement, incumbent status and project status when those facts affect the score; typed facts take precedence over text.

blocker_status.description: Ask whether any blocker is present. A confirmed typed fact overrides word reading.

economic_buyer_engagement.description: Ask whether the budget holder actively participates in this decision. Overrides word reading.

incumbent_status.description: Ask whether the buyer already uses a competing supplier. Overrides word reading.

project_status.description: Ask whether the project is still active. A cancelled project is held, without a close plan.

days_in_stage.description: Days the deal has been in current stage

economic_buyer.description: Economic buyer name and engagement level

competitors.description: Competitors in the deal and their position

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Deal Strategy Coach

tools.name: discovery_question_bank
tools.description: Helps you decide what to ask on a discovery call. You give the framework you use (MEDDPICC, BANT, SPICED, Challenger, Gap Selling or all five) and what you already know about the prospect. You get an opening for the conversation, questions in the language of the prospect's sector and on what your solution covers, questions for each part of the framework, a closing and what to say to an objection. It uses only the inputs you give and says which it did not get.

contact_permission.description: Optional confirmed fact. Ask whether this person permits further contact; this answer overrides contact-refusal wording in the notes.

prospect_role.description: Role of person you are meeting with

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Discovery Question Bank

tools.name: roi_business_case_builder
tools.description: Helps you decide whether the buyer's CFO will accept your ROI case. You give your solution, its main value driver and the buyer's own figures: an annual value estimate, or current annual cost with the expected improvement percent. With them you get the ROI, payback, three year value and sensitivity. Without them it shows no ROI: it names the inputs to add and gives the structure of the case (the cost lines to price, your quoted results as reference points, the questions to ask). Ask finance for the cash-only annual benefit when an investment decision depends on cash.

industry.description: The customer's industry, in any words. Used for wording and sector notes only: no industry figure is applied to the calculation. A return needs the buyer's own figures (annual value estimate, or current annual cost with expected improvement percent)

annual_revenue.description: Customer annual revenue. Shown as your input; it is not turned into a value

employee_count.description: Number of employees. Shown as your input; it is not turned into a value

known_metrics.description: Metrics the prospect shared, or results you can quote. Listed as reference points, never as the buyer's figures; to turn the buyer's figures into the value, give current annual cost and expected improvement percent, or annual value estimate

current_annual_cost.description: Optional: what the problem or the current process costs the buyer a year, in dollars (their figure)

expected_improvement_percent.description: Optional: the share of that annual cost the buyer expects to save, in percent (their figure)

annual_value_estimate.description: Optional: the buyer's own estimate of the annual value in dollars; used as the value when given

current_process.description: How they do it today. Separate the ways of working with a semicolon: each becomes a cost line to price. Not used in the calculation

implementation_timeline.description: Expected implementation time. Shown in the output; not used in the calculation

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

annual_cash_benefit.description: Optional buyer-confirmed annual cash benefit in US dollars, excluding staff time without a cash release. Ask finance to separate cash from non-cash value. Compared with the annual solution price; a cash deficit holds the investment decision.

tools.title: ROI Business Case Builder

tools.name: mutual_action_plan_generator
tools.description: Helps you decide what has to happen, by whom and when, for a deal to sign on time. You give the deal name and the target close date, plus the current stage, the buyer's champion, economic buyer and evaluators, known requirements and process steps if you have them. You get a close plan both sides can work from, with milestones, owners and dates.

target_close_date.description: Target close date (YYYY-MM-DD). A Saturday or Sunday date moves to the Friday before, and the plan says so

known_process_steps.description: Known steps in their buying process, separated by semicolons or new lines (for example: Pilot; security review; procurement). Each step becomes its own milestone

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Mutual Action Plan Generator

tools.name: win_loss_analyzer
tools.description: Helps you decide why you won or lost and what to change. You give the details of one deal, a competitor pattern or a set of deals. You get a short write up that names the outcome, the stated reason in the buyer's words, what the reason points to and what the buyer weighed, then questions for the review call and sector notes. It adds no figure or reason you did not give, and says what a missing outcome or reason would add.

deal_outcome.description: Deal outcome for single deal analysis

deal_details.description: Deal details, can be rough notes, CRM export, or structured data

multiple_deals.description: For portfolio analysis: summary of multiple deals

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Win/Loss Analyzer

tools.name: proposal_section_writer
tools.description: Helps you write one section of a proposal for a named buyer. You give the section you need (such as an executive summary, solution overview or pricing justification), your solution, the buyer's challenges, your differentiators, pricing and success measures. You get that section in sentences built from your inputs, with sector notes. It invents no figure, customer or date, and says once which inputs were not given.

primary_audience.description: Adds a one-line note at the top of the executive summary on what this audience looks for

tone.description: Tone for the proposal (changes only the opening of the executive summary)

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Proposal Section Writer

tools.name: email_sequence_generator
tools.description: Helps you decide what to send, and when, to open or restart a conversation. You give the persona, stage and objective (prospecting, nurture, follow up or re engagement), plus your solution, the pain point, value proposition, proof and ask. You get each email with its subject, send day and body, and a note on what you did not give. No placeholder is left in a body, and no result or statistic is invented.

sequence_type.description: Type of email sequence. cold_outreach, warm_follow_up, post_demo and re_engagement have their own templates; the other types return a general outline

target_persona.description: Target persona (e.g., VP Sales, CTO, CFO)

social_proof.description: Customer names, stats, or proof points

num_emails.description: Accepted but not used yet: each sequence type has a fixed number of emails

sender_context.description: Context about sender (role, shared connections, etc.)

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Email Sequence Generator

tools.name: demo_script_builder
tools.description: Helps you decide what to show in a demo, and in what order. You give the demo type, the persona and the use case, plus the features you must show and the pains you name. You get a timed run from opening to close, with spoken lines and a step for each feature tied to the pains, then discussion, close and follow up lines and sector notes. The answer says where each step came from and what it did not get.

key_pain_points.description: Pain points to address in demo

desired_outcome.description: What you want to achieve from this demo

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Demo Script Builder

tools.name: pricing_negotiation_guide
tools.description: Helps you decide how to answer a discount request without giving away margin. You give the negotiation scenario, plus deal value, the discount asked, each side's leverage and who approves. You get a leverage assessment, a value based negotiation strategy, answers to common pushback and a discount approval framework. Ask whether the user has authority to approve the proposed terms.

your_solution.description: Your product/solution. Named in the guide and used, with your leverage, to read the sector and how you charge

value_delivered.description: Quantified value your solution delivers. Used in the value reframe, word for word; the guide adds no value figure of its own

buyer_leverage.description: Buyer leverage points (size, reference potential, etc.)

your_leverage.description: Your leverage points (unique features, timeline, etc.)

decision_timeline.description: When decision needs to be made

approval_authority.description: Who has final approval on pricing

business_model.description: Optional: how you charge (software subscription, services, connectivity, per transaction, marketplace, hardware plus software, or investment management). Read from your other inputs when left out

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

pricing_authority_status.description: Optional confirmed fact. Ask whether the user can approve this price or discount. Free-text role titles do not establish authority; unconfirmed authority holds commitment to terms.

tools.title: Pricing Negotiation Guide

tools.name: champion_enablement_kit
tools.description: Helps you give your champion what they need to sell internally. You give the asset you need (an executive brief, internal business case, objection responses or presentation talking points), your solution, the customer's situation and the objections you expect. You get the asset in the champion's voice with the recommendation, answers to likely questions, the decision requested, a note on the reader and sector notes. It invents no figure or quote.

target_stakeholder.description: Who the champion needs to convince

champion_wins.description: How this makes the champion look good

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Champion Enablement Kit

tools.name: competitive_trap_setter
tools.description: Helps you decide which questions expose the gaps in your main competitor, without negative selling. You give the named competitor, your solution, your strengths and its weak points as you know them. You get the set up, discovery questions, criteria to establish, reference call questions, requirement and scenario traps, commercial terms and tactics for your stage, with sector notes. Every line comes from your inputs and the sector, and none from an invented fact about the competitor.

buyer_priorities.description: What the buyer cares most about

business_model.description: Optional: how you charge (software subscription, services, connectivity, per transaction, marketplace, hardware plus software, or investment management). Read from your other inputs when left out

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Competitive Trap Setter
